question: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder in teenagers. Here body weight:
solution:
The correct answer is __**loses drastically**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anorexia Nervosa:**

 
 
• Anorexia nervosa is a serious eating disorder characterized by an intense fear of gaining weight, a distorted body image, and persistent behavior that interferes with weight gain.
 
• Individuals with anorexia nervosa severely restrict their food intake, often leading to drastic weight loss.
 
• They may also engage in excessive exercise or use purging behaviors (such as vomiting or laxative abuse) to control their weight.
 
• This disorder can have severe physical and psychological consequences.
 
• It is a mental health condition with a high mortality rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **does not change:**

 
 
• In anorexia nervosa, body weight does not remain stable.
 
• The core feature of the disorder is a drive for thinness, leading to weight loss.
 
• If a persons weight does not change, then they do not have anorexia nervosa.
 
• Weight change is a key diagnostic factor.
 
• This answer is the opposite of the reality of the disorder.
 
 
 
• **increases slightly:**
 
 
• Slight weight gain is not characteristic of anorexia nervosa.
 
• The disorder is defined by a fear of weight gain and behaviors aimed at preventing it.
 
• Any weight gain causes severe distress to a person with anorexia nervosa.
 
• This answer is contrary to the defining characteristics of the illness.
 
• Weight gain is what people with this illness fear.
 
 
 
• **increases drastically:**
 
 
• Drastic weight gain is not associated with anorexia nervosa.
 
• The disorder leads to significant weight loss due to severe food restriction.
 
• Drastic weight increase is associated with other eating disorders.
 
• This is the opposite of the effect of anorexia nervosa.
